text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000076's 99215 rate is elevated in every complexity stratum, but the returned charts largely support the billed levels, so the pattern is inconclusive rather than clearly upcoding or clearly a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The returned charts point away from upcoding: documented 99215 claims were unsupported only slightly more often than at comparison providers, and supported examples such as C0036170 are on genuinely complex patients. The by-complexity table cuts the other way. The provider's 99215 share runs roughly two to three times the all-provider share even among patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, which is exactly where panel acuity cannot explain it. Sampled low-complexity 99215s such as C0036016 (Z09 follow-up only), C0036411 (J06.9 upper respiratory infection) and C0036554 (R10.9 abdominal pain) are the kind of visits that would be unusual at the highest level. Without an audit trail, the documentation itself cannot be fully trusted, given the problems flag, late notes and roughly one in six notes with a repeated time entry; the data-reviewed mismatch affects only 2 notes and is weak. A reviewer should first check whether any documented 99215s fall on 0–1 condition patients and pull charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, then request the EHR audit trail to test whether supporting notes were templated or cloned."}
